_comment: Per-brand import column mappings for the Specials Import screen.

_instructions_for_ai.purpose: This file configures how the Price File Builder app maps a supplier's specials spreadsheet into the RxOne specials grid. Each top-level key (except keys starting with '_') is a brand entry. When the user selects a brand in the Import Specials screen and clicks Import, the app uses that brand's entry to automatically map columns and derive fields.
how_to_add_a_new_brand: 1. Find the exact brand name from the Access Brand table. Query: SELECT BrandID, BrandName FROM Brand ORDER BY BrandName. The JSON key must match BrandName exactly (case-sensitive).
2. Open the supplier's specials file and note the column header names. If there are title/metadata rows above the header row, count them and set skip_rows accordingly.
3. Add a new entry to this file using the schema described below.
4. Validate JSON syntax before saving — missing commas or brackets will prevent the app from loading any mappings.
5. Rebuild the exe via PyInstaller for the change to take effect in a deployed installation. In development it takes effect on next app launch.

schema._description: Optional human-readable note about the brand or file format. Not used by the app.
schema.skip_rows: Optional integer. Number of leading rows in the file to skip before the column header row. Default = 0 (first row is the header). Example: Vantage Gold files have a 4-row title block so skip_rows = 4.

columns._note: Each key is a field role used internally by the app. The value is the column header name in the supplier's file (matched case-insensitively). All roles are optional — omit any that are not present in the file.
columns.barcode: Barcode or EAN. Multiple barcodes in one cell may be comma-separated; all are preserved joined by commas. Can also be a Pharmacode if no barcode is available.
columns.description: Product name/description. Truncated to 40 characters to match the RxOne field limit.
columns.pos_note: Point-of-sale note text printed on receipts or shelf tickets.
columns.multibuy: Minimum quantity required to qualify for the deal (e.g. 2 for 'buy 2 get 1 free').
columns.multibuy_fallback: Fallback quantity column used only when multibuy is empty for a row (e.g. a separate 'Quantity breaks' column for X-for-$Y deals).
columns.deal_name: Name of the deal or promotion. Used by the sequential_by_deal_name group_id rule to assign sequential Group IDs to rows that share the same deal. Can also be a supplier/category name if grouping by supplier is desired.
columns.product_price: Direct special retail price as a dollar amount (e.g. 4.99). Takes priority over discount-based price calculation. Maps to the Special Price column in the grid.
columns.discount_type: Type of discount. Currently only '%' is handled — if the value is '%' and product_price is empty, the app formats discount_value as a percentage string (e.g. '50%').
columns.discount_value: Numeric discount amount. Used together with discount_type when no product_price is available.
columns.special_name: Promotion or special name. Read from the first data row only and used to pre-fill the Special Name text field at the bottom of the Import Specials screen.
columns.start_date: Promotion start date. Read from the first data row only to pre-fill the Start Date picker. Must be ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD) or a similar pandas-parseable date string.
columns.end_date: Promotion end date. Read from the first data row only to pre-fill the Finish Date picker. Same format requirements as start_date.

rules._note: Rules control fields that are derived from logic rather than read directly from a column. All rules have defaults and are optional.

group_id.sequential_by_deal_name: Assign a sequential integer Group ID to each unique deal_name value encountered in the file. First unique deal name = 1, second = 2, etc. All rows sharing the same deal name get the same Group ID. Rows with no deal name get no Group ID. Use this when the file has a deal/promotion name column.
group_id.from_column:<col>: Read the Group ID value directly from the named column in the file. Replace <col> with the exact column header. Example: 'from_column:Product A or B'.

flybuys.true: All rows get Flybuys = Y. Use only when every product in the brand's specials participates in the Flybuys loyalty scheme.

lowest_free.disc_pct_and_multibuy_gt1: Set Get Lowest Free = Y only when BOTH: discount_type is '%' AND MultiBuy Qty > 1. Covers the typical 'buy 2, cheapest item % off' scenario.
lowest_free.always_false: All rows get Get Lowest Free = N. Use for simple price specials with no multibuy/free-item mechanic.
lowest_free.from_column:<col>: Read the flag from the named column. Values Y, YES, TRUE, or 1 (case-insensitive) map to Y; anything else maps to N.

special_price.product_price_then_disc_pct: Use product_price column if it has a value (dollar amount). Otherwise, if discount_type is '%', format discount_value as a percentage string (e.g. '50%'). If neither is available, Special Price is left blank.
special_price.direct_column:<col>: Read Special Price directly from the named column with no further calculation. Use when the file already contains the final formatted price string.

worked_examples.flat_price_list_with_title_block: See 'Vantage Gold' — file has 4 metadata rows before the header (skip_rows: 4), direct CTC price, no multibuy, grouped by Supplier column.
worked_examples.mixed_price_and_percent_with_dates: See 'GXH' — file has named-header columns for price, percentage discount, multibuy qty, deal grouping, and promotion dates. Lowest Free derived automatically.

_instructions_for_ai.column_resolution_priority: For each field the app tries: (1) brand mapping column value, (2) built-in known header names (e.g. 'Barcodes', 'Product name', 'Promotion POS note'), (3) manual column-number combo set by the user in the UI. Brand mapping takes priority over all.
